# Shared AI client

`@katalon-experiments/ai-client` sends serialized OpenAI Responses directly
to `https://api.openai.com/v1` using `OPENAI_API_KEY`. OpenRouter is used only
for native JEV System One and its TypeSafe endpoint catalog, using
`LOKI_OPENROUTER_API_KEY` or `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`. Keys are independent.

```js
import { providerConnection, sendFetch } from "@katalon-experiments/ai-client";
const connection = providerConnection(
  "https://api.openai.com/v1/responses",
  process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY,
);
const response = await sendFetch(connection, {
  method: "POST",
  body: existingSerializedNativeRequest,
  signal: existingAbortSignal,
});
```

The client preserves serialized bytes, model/reasoning fields, native responses,
usage, errors, streaming and cancellation. It adds no retries, replay, model
selection or success interpretation. `providerConnection` refuses embeddings,
OpenRouter Responses, arbitrary endpoints and credential-bearing URLs.

`LOKI_LITELLM_ENABLED` and `LOKI_LITELLM_ORIGIN` cannot redirect these native
routes. Their historical parsers, convenience client and embeddings route are retained
in `experiments/2173-reasoning-support/provider-transport`; Product exports only
its selected native serialized transport and accounting helpers. The native profile requires provider keys; the separately selected managed Codex host is described below. Fetch redirects are refused;
Node HTTP requests do not follow redirects. Inherited Authorization is replaced
with the credential for the selected native endpoint.

Callers with exact serialization and evidence contracts use
`providerConnection(nativeUrl, key, env)` plus `sendFetch` or `requestHttp`.
Their original bounded readers, deadlines, Stop, partial-byte retention and
unknown-charge rules remain in their own components. `lunaUsageEstimate` derives
standard-tier costs from valid native usage using official Luna rates checked
30 October 2026. The caller must label that value as an estimate rather than a
billing receipt. Missing/invalid usage returns null, never an invented zero.

Consumers bundle this dependency into their immutable package. Run `npm test`
for controlled transport tests; these do not make paid inference calls or prove
live-provider acceptance. Historical archives and experiment entrypoints are
not migrated by this change. Hai's routing decision is recorded in
[#2161](https://github.com/katalon-studio/loki/issues/2161#issuecomment-6517382712).

## Managed Codex host

A host-bound `LOKI_AUTH_BROKER_SOCKET` selects the private Unix channel for the
Codex shared-auth build. This is a public local address, not a provider credential.
The broker owns OAuth and forwards the explicit operation through Core to LiteLLM.
`sendFetch` and `requestHttp` retain serialization, cancellation and streaming;
channel failure never switches to the direct route. Without that host binding,
the native OpenAI/JEV behavior above remains unchanged. Existing legacy LiteLLM
flags still cannot redirect calls. See [the Product contract](../../docs/product-design/codex-shared-auth.md).
